newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cosipa says exports halted by port protest.
newsitem.headline: Cosipa says exports halted by port protest.

text.p: Brazilian steelmaker Cosipa said a two-week-old protest by stevedores at its Santos port loading terminal halted exports and hurt its steel output capacity.
A company spokeswoman said Cosipa has not been able to export steel since workers occupied two ships April 2 at its Santos terminal while a lack of iron imports has affected capacity at its mill.
The workers were ousted by federal police early Tuesday morning but not before fellow Santos stevedores called a strike for 0700 local time, paralyzing Latin America's largest port.

In protest, between 500 and 2,000 workers blocked the terminal's entrance road and burned tires outside the Cosipa terminal. The workers were protesting a company decision to use private employees to load and unload ships instead of unionized stevedores.
The spokeswoman said she did not know how much the protest had affected the company's balance sheet.
Cosipa exports an average 100,000 tonnes of steel per month totalling $35 million in revenue, she said.
She also said the lack of imports has required Cosipa to alter its blend of materials to produce steel, affecting production capacity at its blast furnace.
Union leaders, meanwhile, said they had offered to load and unload for free any materials needed to keep Cosipa's production going but the offer was rejected.
